title: android:debuggable="true" set explicitly on <application>
sink: JDWP debugger attach / `adb shell run-as <pkg>` shell access to the app sandbox
sanitizer_notes: No evidence of a release-variant build flag or manifest-merger override stripping this attribute; it is set as a literal, unconditional value in the manifest under audit.

evidence.detail: AndroidManifest.xml <application> tag: android:name=".VulnBankApp" android:allowBackup="true" android:debuggable="true" android:label="VulnBank Demo" ... (lines 7-13 of extracted/AndroidManifest.xml)

Attempted the finding's own suggested command verbatim against the connected device 84f7a024 (Xiaomi Redmi "sweetin"/M2101K6P, Android 11 / SDK 30, build Redmi/sweetin/sweetin:11/RKQ1.200826.002/V12.5.10.0.RKFINXM:user/release-keys): `adb shell run-as com.vulnbankdemo.app id` -> actual output: `run-as: unknown package: com.vulnbankdemo.app` (exit code 1). Independently cross-checked with `adb shell pm list packages | grep -i vulnbank` (no match out of 389 installed packages) and `adb shell dumpsys package com.vulnbankdemo.app` (output: `Unable to find package: com.vulnbankdemo.app`). All three independently confirm com.vulnbankdemo.app has never been installed on the only available test device. The debuggable=true manifest declaration therefore remains static-only: it cannot be runtime-confirmed (JDWP attach / run-as shell) without first building an installable package from this manifest, which does not exist. For baseline-only context (not a substitute for testing the app itself), the device's own OS build is a production image (`ro.debuggable=0`, `ro.secure=1`) -- this says nothing about the target app's manifest attribute, which is a separate, per-APK setting.

reproduction_static: 1. Open the decoded AndroidManifest.xml. 2. Confirm android:debuggable="true" is present on the <application> element (not a tool-injected default -- apktool/aapt only emit this when it is actually set, e.g. via a debug build variant or explicit manifest entry). 3. Cross-check against any available build.gradle (none exists for this fixture) to see which build type set it.

If an installable build matching this manifest becomes available, confirm with `adb shell run-as com.vulnbankdemo.app id` (succeeds without root if debuggable) and/or jdb/`adb shell am attach-debugger` against the forwarded JDWP port -- suggested for dynamic-runtime-verifier per MAN-18. No APK/installable package exists for this fixture today, so this cannot be executed now.
final_rating_reason: Panel: prosecutor's case (exploitation/AND-MAN-001.md) stands; both skeptic-1 and skeptic-2 independently returned stands with specific checks performed (attacker-model inflation, missed sanitizer, SDK-version mitigation, standard-behavior misread, evidence quality, ADB-precondition realism) and no well-evidenced refuted. Orchestrator applying severity-rating.md's Confirmed bar: no dynamic PoC exists (the real adb session against device 84f7a024 confirmed com.vulnbankdemo.app is not installed, so run-as/JDWP was never actually exercised against a live process), and the static proof is not fully unambiguous either since a genuine open conditional remains unresolved -- whether a release-build override would force debuggable=false, which cannot be checked either way because no build.gradle exists anywhere in this fixture. That combination (static-only reachability, device/build to dynamically confirm unavailable) matches the Potential tier's definition exactly, not Confirmed's. Severity kept at the prosecutor's proposed high: uncontested by either skeptic, and the asset is banking-grade per the app's own component/label naming (.ui.TransferMoneyActivity, .data.AccountProvider, label "VulnBank Demo"), which is the stated exception to the resilience-finding Low/Info default.
notes: target-profile.md flags this as explicitly set (not a decompiler artifact). If this manifest reflects a genuinely shipped release build, debuggable=true permits debugger attachment and run-as shell access, undermining every other control; if it is actually a non-release/test build, the finding stands against *this* build specifically. This is a hand-authored fixture manifest (no APK/source exists) -- treat confidence accordingly, but the declaration itself is the audit target, not an extraction artifact.

title: android:allowBackup="true" with no backup-content restriction on a banking app
source: android:allowBackup="true" on <application>; no android:fullBackupContent; no android:dataExtractionRules
sink: `adb backup`/cloud auto-backup extraction of the app's private data directory (SharedPreferences, SQLite DBs, files)
sanitizer_notes: No fullBackupContent XML or dataExtractionRules XML is referenced anywhere in the manifest to exclude sensitive files (e.g. session tokens, cached account data) from backup; no attribute narrows the default full-data backup.

evidence.detail: <application android:name=".VulnBankApp" android:allowBackup="true" android:debuggable="true" android:label="VulnBank Demo" ...> -- no fullBackupContent/dataExtractionRules attribute present anywhere in the file (lines 7-13).

Attempted the finding's own suggested command against the connected device 84f7a024 (Xiaomi Redmi "sweetin"/M2101K6P, Android 11 / SDK 30, build Redmi/sweetin/sweetin:11/RKQ1.200826.002/V12.5.10.0.RKFINXM:user/release-keys): `adb backup -noapk com.vulnbankdemo.app`. adb printed the standard deprecation warning and initiated the on-device BackupRestoreConfirmation flow, which blocks waiting for a manual unlock + on-screen confirmation tap (and optional backup-password entry) -- it does not pre-check package existence before prompting. This cannot be completed non-interactively; it was deliberately not forced through for two reasons: (1) com.vulnbankdemo.app is confirmed not installed on this device (see AND-MAN-001/004/005 dynamic evidence), so a completed backup would contain nothing relevant to this finding regardless; (2) this is a shared physical test device with other, unrelated apps installed (observed during `pm list packages`: e.g. com.app.damnvulnerablebank, com.catalent.onehub.dev.debug) that are explicitly out of scope per scope.md, and blindly automating a physical confirmation tap without screen visibility risks interacting with the wrong on-screen element. The confirmation dialog was cleanly dismissed via `adb shell input keyevent KEYCODE_BACK`; verified via `adb shell dumpsys activity activities | grep mResumedActivity` that the device returned to its prior foreground activity with no backup file produced and no app data touched.

reproduction_static: 1. Inspect <application> for the allowBackup value and absence of fullBackupContent/dataExtractionRules. 2. Confirm no backup_rules.xml/data_extraction_rules.xml is referenced anywhere in the manifest.
reproduction_dynamic:
ATTEMPTED 2026-10-09 against device 84f7a024 (Xiaomi Redmi "sweetin"/M2101K6P, Android 11 / SDK 30, build Redmi/sweetin/sweetin:11/RKQ1.200826.002/V12.5.10.0.RKFINXM:user/release-keys): `adb backup -noapk com.vulnbankdemo.app` triggered the on-device backup-confirmation dialog but could not be completed non-interactively (requires a physical unlock+tap this session cannot safely automate on a shared device) and the target package is confirmed not installed regardless. Dialog was cleanly dismissed afterward; no backup artifact was produced. Original suggested reproduction preserved below.

On a device with this app installed and USB debugging enabled: `adb backup -noapk com.vulnbankdemo.app` then inspect the resulting tarball for app_data contents -- suggested for dynamic-runtime-verifier (MAN-18) once an installable build exists; not executable against this manifest-only fixture today.
notes: Given the app's apparent purpose (banking/money transfer, per .ui.TransferMoneyActivity and .data.AccountProvider class names), any session tokens or cached account data stored locally would be subject to backup extraction by anyone with physical/ADB access to an unlocked, debugging-enabled device. Severity would rise if storage-crypto-auditor confirms sensitive data is actually persisted unencrypted -- cross-reference that specialist's output when available.

title: TransferMoneyActivity exported with BROWSABLE custom-scheme deep link and no permission guard
source: Any installed app, or a web page/link opened in a mobile browser (category BROWSABLE), sending/navigating to an Intent with action=VIEW, data=vulnbank://transfer
sink: TransferMoneyActivity's Intent-handling code (onCreate/onNewIntent) -- implementation not present in this manifest-only artifact, but the class name strongly implies a money-movement action
sanitizer_notes: No android:permission attribute on the <activity>; no custom <permission> is defined anywhere in the manifest, so there is no signature-level gate even available to apply; no android:autoVerify / https App Link verification is used for this scheme (it is a bare custom scheme, not a verified App Link), so scheme-collision by another installed app is also possible in addition to direct exposure.

evidence.detail: Ran the finding's own suggested command verbatim against the connected device 84f7a024 (Xiaomi Redmi "sweetin"/M2101K6P, Android 11 / SDK 30, build Redmi/sweetin/sweetin:11/RKQ1.200826.002/V12.5.10.0.RKFINXM:user/release-keys) on 2026-10-09: `adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d "vulnbank://transfer" com.vulnbankdemo.app` -> actual output: `Error: Activity not started, unable to resolve Intent { act=android.intent.action.VIEW dat=vulnbank://transfer flg=0x10000000 pkg=com.vulnbankdemo.app }`. Also re-ran as a bare implicit intent with no explicit package (`adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d "vulnbank://transfer"`) to test whether any other installed app on this device claims the vulnbank:// scheme -- same resolution failure, confirming no component on this device (not just not com.vulnbankdemo.app) currently registers for this scheme. This dynamically confirms the premise the finding's own reproduction_dynamic already stated prospectively ('no APK/installable package exists... cannot be executed now') -- re-verified today rather than merely inherited from target-profile.md -- but it does NOT confirm or refute TransferMoneyActivity's actual runtime behavior (whether reaching it executes a transfer without a fresh auth/confirmation step). That question, identified as the case's central open gap in exploitation/AND-MAN-003.md, remains exactly as unresolved as before: it requires real implementation code or an installable build, neither of which exists for this fixture. Status/final_severity (potential/high, set by the orchestrator) are left untouched by this dynamic pass -- nothing observed today moves the needle on the impact-side gap the skeptics already identified.

reproduction_static: 1. Locate <activity android:name=".ui.TransferMoneyActivity"> in the manifest. 2. Confirm android:exported="true" and the absence of android:permission. 3. Confirm the intent-filter carries BROWSABLE plus a custom scheme/host (vulnbank://transfer), making it reachable both from any other installed app via an explicit/implicit Intent and from a mobile browser via an intent:// or vulnbank:// link.
reproduction_dynamic:
ATTEMPTED 2026-10-09 against device 84f7a024 (Xiaomi Redmi "sweetin"/M2101K6P, Android 11 / SDK 30, build Redmi/sweetin/sweetin:11/RKQ1.200826.002/V12.5.10.0.RKFINXM:user/release-keys) (both `pkg=com.vulnbankdemo.app`-qualified and bare implicit forms): both returned `Error: Activity not started, unable to resolve Intent`, confirming no component on this device currently claims the vulnbank:// scheme. This re-confirms (does not newly discover) that no installable build exists; it does not resolve the still-open question of whether the activity executes a transfer without re-authentication, since no implementation code or installed build exists to observe. Original suggested reproduction preserved below.

Suggested for dynamic-runtime-verifier if a stub/installable APK is ever built from this manifest (none exists today, per target-profile.md): `adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d "vulnbank://transfer" com.vulnbankdemo.app` and, separately, host an HTML page with `<a href="vulnbank://transfer">` opened in a mobile browser, to confirm the activity launches without any prompt/permission check (MAN-18). Also worth a drozer `app.activity.start` / `app.activity.info` pass.
final_rating_reason: Reachability is unambiguous static proof (exported, BROWSABLE, no permission infrastructure anywhere in the manifest); both independent skeptics stand on that. But both also name a plausible, unresolved conditional neither could rule out: an in-app confirmation/auth step before a transfer actually executes, unverifiable because no implementation code exists for this fixture. Per severity-rating.md, a plausible unresolved conditional on static-only evidence caps this at Potential, not Confirmed.
notes: Exported-ness alone would not be a finding (deep-link entry activities are often intentionally public), but the combination of (a) a money-transfer-implying name, (b) zero permission guard, and (c) BROWSABLE web-reachability pushes attacker_model to 'remote' at minimum per the escalation rule (any webpage can fire an intent:// link). Hand off the actual Intent-extra parsing/validation question (does it require prior auth state, does it trust extras blindly, is there a confirmation screen) to android-ipc-ui-auditor and taint-flow-analyst; also cross-reference deeplink-clipboard-auditor's DLK-01..08 checks (clipboard-webview-oauth.md) and WEB-11 for the webpage-triggered angle. No implementation code exists in this fixture to confirm actual impact -- this finding is scoped to the manifest-level exposure only.

title: AccountProvider exported with no permission, no path-permission, no URI scoping
source: Any installed app issuing a ContentResolver query()/insert()/update()/delete() against content://com.vulnbankdemo.app.provider, no permission required
sink: AccountProvider's query/insert/update/delete implementation (not present in this manifest-only artifact); the class name implies it backs account/financial data
sanitizer_notes: No android:readPermission, android:writePermission, or android:permission attribute on the <provider>; no <path-permission> child elements to narrow exposure by sub-path; no android:grantUriPermissions scoping (moot here since the entire authority is already unrestricted); single flat authority with no path segmentation at all.

evidence.detail: <provider android:name=".data.AccountProvider" android:authorities="com.vulnbankdemo.app.provider" android:exported="true" /> (lines 35-38) -- no child elements, no permission attributes of any kind.

Ran the finding's own suggested command verbatim against the connected device 84f7a024 (Xiaomi Redmi "sweetin"/M2101K6P, Android 11 / SDK 30, build Redmi/sweetin/sweetin:11/RKQ1.200826.002/V12.5.10.0.RKFINXM:user/release-keys) on 2026-10-09: `adb shell content query --uri content://com.vulnbankdemo.app.provider` -> actual output: `Error while accessing provider:com.vulnbankdemo.app.provider` / `java.lang.IllegalStateException: Could not find provider: com.vulnbankdemo.app.provider`. Confirms AccountProvider is not registered on this device because com.vulnbankdemo.app is not installed (consistent with the pm list / dumpsys / run-as results recorded under AND-MAN-001/005/006). The unauthenticated read/write question this finding raises (what data is actually returned/mutated, whether raw-SQL selection/sortOrder injection is possible) remains entirely unverified -- it requires AccountProvider's implementation code or an installed build, neither of which exists for this fixture.

reproduction_static: 1. Locate <provider android:name=".data.AccountProvider"> in the manifest. 2. Confirm android:exported="true" with no android:readPermission/writePermission/permission attribute and no <path-permission> children. 3. Note the authority string for use in a content:// URI.

ATTEMPTED 2026-10-09 against device 84f7a024 (Xiaomi Redmi "sweetin"/M2101K6P, Android 11 / SDK 30, build Redmi/sweetin/sweetin:11/RKQ1.200826.002/V12.5.10.0.RKFINXM:user/release-keys): `adb shell content query --uri content://com.vulnbankdemo.app.provider` -> `IllegalStateException: Could not find provider: com.vulnbankdemo.app.provider`. Suggested for dynamic-runtime-verifier if an installable build is ever produced (none exists today): `adb shell content query --uri content://com.vulnbankdemo.app.provider` and the corresponding insert/update/delete variants, run from an unprivileged shell, to confirm what data is actually returned/mutated without holding any permission (MAN-18).
